review.tagline: Pipeline that builds knowledge graphs from text for LLM question answering
review.summary: GraphRAG is a Python data pipeline from Microsoft Research that uses an LLM to extract structured data from unstructured text and form a knowledge graph. That graph is used to build context for question answering over private data. It runs from a command line (`graphrag init`, indexing, querying) with configurable settings and tunable prompts. The project is in maintenance mode: bug fixes and dependency updates only.
review.audience: Engineers experimenting with graph-based RAG over private document collections
strengths: Backed by a published paper (arXiv 2404.16130) and a Microsoft Research blog post
Prompt tuning guide for adapting extraction to your own data
Installable from PyPI, with a CLI quickstart and hosted documentation
MIT license, with a release in September 2026
weaknesses: Maintenance mode: no new features and no new PRs accepted
Indexing can be expensive in LLM calls; README advises starting small
Not an officially supported Microsoft offering; code is a demonstration
Config format changes between versions require re-running `graphrag init --force`
